title: R4-C0 pre-registration: region over-segmentation + region adjacency graph + hierarchical merging (training-free POC). Committed before any Gate 1-4 run.
no_training: no new model, no change to M1 / M2 / B2 weights; the frozen weights are only run in inference
change_policy: Each gate runs once. After this commit only crash / implementation-bug fixes are allowed, documented with the reason. No change of over-segmentation, strength definitions, grids, selection rules, thresholds, sheets or metrics after seeing any result. If RAG fails, M2_hybrid is kept and no second region-graph algorithm is tried in R4-C0.
corrections_of_earlier_wording: R4-B0 Gate 3 values 0.823 / 0.783 (M1 probability terrain) and 0.740 / 0.714 (M2 distance) use ideal seeds derived from the official instances: they are ORACLE upper bounds, not deployable autonomous results. The route review sentence that only changing seeds could raise 0.596 to about 0.82 overstated this; it shows headroom, not an achievable autonomous gain.
Superpixel ASA, under-segmentation error and majority-label assignment are not the small-instance IoU >= 0.5 recall and are never reported as such.

literature_basis.owt_ucm: Arbeláez et al. 2011: contours -> initial regions (oriented watershed) -> hierarchy by boundary strength (UCM). R4-C0 uses a simplified, non-oriented version: watershed on a boundary map + greedy merging by the MEDIAN pair strength of the shared border. It is NOT a reimplementation of OWT-UCM; the median (not mean) is chosen to limit contamination by a few strong or weak pixels along the border.
literature_basis.superpixel_benchmark: ASA (achievable segmentation accuracy) and under-segmentation error (UE, Neubert / Achanta style, min(inside, outside) per region-instance overlap) as defined in the Stutz et al. superpixel benchmark; reported only as region-quality measures

inputs.training_sheets: freeze_config.json data_roles.train (10 sheets): Gate 1 and Gate 2 only
inputs.training_sheet_predictions: the frozen M1 / M2 / B2 best.pt are run in inference on the 10 training sheets (experiments/R4A/r4a2_2_infer.py for M1 and M2, experiments/R4B2/r4b2_infer.py for B2). These are IN-SAMPLE predictions: they are cleaner than on unseen sheets, so oracles and selected thresholds may be optimistic; Gate 3 checks this on held-out sheets.
inputs.dev_sheets: 15023, 15041 (DEVELOPMENT_VALIDATION; also used for checkpoint selection of all three models); existing R4-A2.2 / R4-B2 predictions
inputs.retrospective: 14030, 13015 (already exposed to M2_hybrid and B2 results): reported as retrospective controls only, never as independent tests
inputs.image_only_at_prediction: prediction uses model outputs and the RGB image only; labels are read only by oracle and metric code

candidates.M1: pixel strength b = M1 boundary probability; pair strength = max(b_p, b_q)
candidates.M2: pixel strength b = M2 boundary-head probability; pair strength = max(b_p, b_q) (the distance head is not used)
candidates.B2: pixel strength b = max of the edge probabilities of the pixel's incident pairs; pair strength = the pair's own edge probability

over_segmentation: one method for all candidates (experiments/R4C0/r4c0_rag.overseg): q = round(255 b) as uint8; markers = 4-connected components of the h-minima of q with h = 13 (0.05 in probability); watershed of q from those markers with 4-connectivity over the full image. No area threshold, no other parameter.
rag: node = initial region; edge = regions sharing >= 1 4-adjacent pixel pair; edge stores a 64-bin histogram of pair strengths over all shared pairs; region stores area and Lab colour sum / count over non-ink pixels (fallback all pixels if < 5 non-ink pixels)

merge.rule: greedy, deterministic: repeatedly merge the adjacent pair with the lowest cost; on merge, histograms and colour sums add and costs of touched edges are recomputed; ties by cost then (i, j)
merge.RAG_BOUNDARY_ONLY: cost = median pair strength on the shared border (64-bin resolution)
merge.RAG_BOUNDARY_APPEARANCE: cost = median pair strength + lambda * min(dE76(mean Lab_i, mean Lab_j) / 30, 1); same initial regions
merge.colour: Lab from the RGB image (cv2, L 0-100); ink = gray black-hat ellipse 9 px > 40, dilated 1 px (image-only, same rule as the label builder's ink); no official class, legend-unit mapping or test label
merge.stop: merging stops at the first popped cost > tau

per_candidate_and_sheet: initial regions (count, mean / median area in valid px)
over-segmentation + RAG build + full merge-sequence time, peak RSS
Oracle A and Oracle B small-instance IoU >= 0.5 recall per width bin (canonical width, experiments/R4B1T/r4b1t_width)
share of small instances already MIXED in the initial regions
large-instance fragmentation: median and 90th percentile of the number of initial regions holding >= 1% of a >= 20000 px instance
gate1.oracle_A: OPTIMISTIC: for each instance alone, the best IoU of any union of initial regions (purity-sorted prefixes, which is optimal for a single target); IGNORES exclusivity (a region may be used for several instances) and connectivity of the union
gate1.oracle_B: ACHIEVABLE truth-assisted merge: every initial region takes its majority instance (valid pixels), adjacent regions with the same majority are merged; regions stay indivisible, each is used once, unions are connected through the region graph
gate1.mixed_definition: a small instance is MIXED if Oracle A best IoU < 0.5 (no union of initial regions reaches IoU 0.5)
gate1.pooling: all small instances of the 10 training sheets pooled; per-sheet values reported
gate1.qualification: a candidate qualifies iff Oracle A recall in the pooled 6-20 px group (bins 6-10 and 10-20 together) >= 0.90 AND per-sheet peak RSS <= 12 GB AND per-sheet time (over-segmentation + RAG + full merge) <= 15 min AND initial regions <= 400000 per sheet
stop: no candidate qualifies -> STOP route one, report the limits
a candidate is computationally infeasible on M4 16 GB -> it is disqualified (no re-tuning)
even if Oracle A >= 0.90, if Oracle B for every qualified candidate is < 0.80 in the 6-20 px group, STOP: the effective merge is not approachable
gate1.3-6px: reported separately; never a reason to stop or to pass

gate2.candidate_selection: among qualified candidates: highest pooled Oracle B recall in the 6-20 px group on the 10 training sheets; tie (< 0.005) -> fewer initial regions
gate2.objective: pooled small-instance IoU >= 0.5 recall on the 10 training sheets (r4a2_2_eval.instance_metrics per sheet, pooled by counts), subject to pooled small over-segmentation <= 0.10; ties (< 0.002) -> lower tau, then lower lambda
gate2.RAG_BOUNDARY_APPEARANCE: (tau, lambda) chosen jointly on tau_grid x lambda_grid with the same objective
gate2.freeze: selected candidate, tau and lambda are committed before Gate 3

gate3.metrics: small recall, 6-10 / 10-20 px recall (and 3-6 separately), multi-instance merges, over-seg, under-seg, regions, large recall, boundary F1@1/2/3, GIS export 9 checks

failure_decomposition_per_failed_small_i.INITIAL_MIXED: Oracle A < 0.5 on this sheet's initial regions
failure_decomposition_per_failed_small_i.MERGE_ERROR: not INITIAL_MIXED, and the best-overlap final region also holds >= 50% of another instance
failure_decomposition_per_failed_small_i.UNDER_MERGE_FRAGMENTS: not INITIAL_MIXED, and no final region holds >= 50% of the instance

gate3.appearance_effect: PREVENTED_MERGE = recovered by APPEARANCE but MERGE_ERROR in BOUNDARY_ONLY; CAUSED_SPLIT = recovered by BOUNDARY_ONLY but UNDER_MERGE_FRAGMENTS in APPEARANCE
gate3.catastrophic_merge: largest predicted region area > 1.5 x the largest official instance area (valid px)
gate3.pass: at least one RAG variant on BOTH dev sheets: small recall >= M2_hybrid + 0.03, small over-seg increase <= 0.03, large recall drop <= 0.05, no catastrophic merge. Otherwise STOP: no new independent sheet is consumed.

gate4.sheet_walk: experiments/R4B1T/gate5_candidates.json from order 11 (15078) onward, skipping every code already visited (13076, 14030, 14071, 15094, 13015) and any code used in any role; unchanged Q1/Q2/Q3 (experiments/R4A/gtf_dataset.process)
gate4.sample_size_rule: after a sheet PASSES Q3 its labels are built and ONLY the number of small instances is counted (no model is run); a PASS sheet with < 100 small instances is logged as INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE and the walk continues; stop at 2 sheets with >= 100 small instances or after 8 visited candidates (then report what was found)
gate4.frozen_before: inference, merge rule, tau, lambda, evaluation code committed before the first download
gate4.success: at least one RAG variant on BOTH new sheets: small recall >= M2_hybrid + 0.03; small over-seg increase <= 0.03; large recall drop <= 0.05; no catastrophic merge; GIS export 9 checks pass
gate4.appearance_report: paired gain APPEARANCE - BOUNDARY_ONLY per sheet with a 95% paired bootstrap CI over small instances (2000 resamples, seed 20261029); if the CI contains 0 -> 'no evidence of independent value yet' (not 'colour is useless')
gate4.uncertainty: per sheet: number of small instances, absolute recall change vs M2_hybrid, 95% paired bootstrap CI

questions: is training-free region-level reconstruction better than M2_hybrid?
is the gain from better initial regions or better merging?
which 6-20 px narrow units are protected?
does appearance add information beyond the boundary model?
next: more GSJ data, a learned region-appearance model, or topology-aware learning?
gate5.if_fail: keep M2_hybrid; no second region-graph algorithm in R4-C0

limits.no_upload: GSJ rasters, official vectors, weights, restricted visuals stay local
